searchText: <kevaundray> @amvlasov on the ACD call, it was noted that matterlabs uses the modexp precompile. Do you know what it is being used for in matterlabs and what bit sizes? In our benchmarks, I believe modexp was one of the worse offenders. Its essentially a function that allows you to do modular exponentiation with upto 8192 bits (reference for others) <amvlasov> We have an implementation that relies on bigint precompile for it's functionality and it's efficient, but so far it's somewhere low in drafts and priority <amvlasov> Or do you mean how we use modexp precompile on L1? <kevaundray> re: **@amvlasov** > Or do you mean how we use modexp precompile on L1? yep on L1 <amvlasov> To the base of my memory it's 64 byte transcript output -> BN254 field element element challenge as suggested by some of the RFCs to get proper uniform challenge. Namely something like `(challenge)^1 mod BN254_Fq_modulus` <kevaundray> re: **@amvlasov** > To the base of my memory it's 64 byte transcript output -> BN254 field element element challenge as suggested by some of the RFCs to get proper uniform challenge. Namely something like (challenge)^1 mod BN254_Fq_modulus Okay this would make sense; so its not really modexp that you want, its really efficient modular reduction from 512 bits to ~254 bits to get a uniform challenge <kevaundray> Where modexp is a superset of this <amvlasov> yes, it can be doen with just long division as Knuth says, but it would require more time and code <kevaundray> re: **@amvlasov** > yes, it can be doen with just long division as Knuth says, but it would require more time and code Would matterlabs be fine if we 3x this? (In the sense that it doesn't break any of your usecases) I imagine that when we reprice things for zkEVMs it will be increased even further <amvlasov> Do you mean gas constants? <kevaundray> re: **@amvlasov** > Do you mean gas constants? Yep, L1 gas price for modexp <amvlasov> We do not hardcode gas limits, so it'll work and not break, but for repricing you should contant @alocascio as he did such investigation for us already. We will not break gas constants, but will use some other mechanism to ensure no attacks on operator from sequencing

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content:
<kevaundray> @amvlasov on the ACD call, it was noted that matterlabs uses the modexp precompile. Do you know what it is being used for in matterlabs and what bit sizes?

In our benchmarks, I believe modexp was one of the worse offenders. 

Its essentially a function that allows you to do modular exponentiation with upto 8192 bits (reference for others)
